title: Nested Contributors can always submit Artifact Edit Proposals without meeting the token threshold
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1 states that "Nested Contributors are always authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and do not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements," while "all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply."

The exemption is precisely scoped: it removes the capital gate, not the review gates. A Nested Contributor's proposal still needs Spark Risk Council review, Operational Facilitator alignment review, and a token holder vote. Only the right to *initiate* is unconditioned.

The rationale follows from what a Nested Contributor is (A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.5): a development company core to both Spark and Sky, such as Phoenix Labs. The parties most likely to identify a needed technical amendment are the engineers, and their compensation does not necessarily include 1% of token supply. Making proposal rights contingent on holdings would silence exactly the constituency with the best information.

The corresponding risk is durable influence not backed by stake: an entity with no minimum economic exposure holds permanent standing to put items on the governance agenda. The Atlas answers that not by limiting the right but by pairing it with a protection running the other direction — SKY holders must also approve any edit that removes a Nested Contributor.
description: Core contributors to both Spark and Sky keep permanent proposal rights independent of their holdings, but remain bound by every other step of the Root Edit process.
